name: CryptoPanic quiet (low bullish votes) + rising price — under-the-radar accumulation (spot long)
rationale: MECHANISM (why low attention + rising price leads): a price that is grinding UP while CryptoPanic bullish votes are still LOW is being accumulated by informed flow before the retail crowd notices — the move is 'under the radar'. The predictive lead is the gap between price action and attention: when the crowd finally arrives (votes surge), the easy gains are late-stage. So we enter on quiet attention (bullish votes below a fitted ceiling) + positive ret_Nd (the quiet uptrend), and EXIT when bullish votes cross UP (the crowd shows up — time to distribute), or stop/TP/time. This is the mirror of the bullish-surge-momentum spec: same feature, opposite regime (absence vs presence of attention). DISCONFIRMER 1: if plain momentum without the low-attention gate matches the deflated Sharpe, the quiet-crowd filter adds nothing. DISCONFIRMER 2: low votes may just mean the coin is illiquid/ignored (no edge, only slippage) — the min_liquidity screen is the guard. Requires CRYPTOPANIC_API_KEY; low-confidence until validated OOS.
catalyst: cryptopanic_bullish_votes stay BELOW a low ceiling (crowd not yet paying attention) while price is quietly rising.
